data.title: Research: best-selling our vintage vinyl records webshop � mine the keyword set products & competitors

data.body: Research complete — Flagging this up front: none of these are vinyl records — they’re a generic dummy-catalog sample (cosmetics and fragrances), so treat this purely as a price-band exercise, not a real vinyl-inventory read. The sample spans roughly $9–$130 in two clear tiers — a budget cluster ($9–$20: mascara, eyeshadow, powder, lipstick, nail polish) and a premium cluster ($50–$130: the designer fragrances) — which maps reasonably well onto real vinyl pricing, where mass-market reissue LPs run $15–$30 and collectible or audiophile/box-set pressings run $50–$150+. If I had to pick 3 analogues to lead with, I’d choose Chanel Coco Noir ($129.99), Dior J’adore ($89.99), and Gucci Bloom ($79.99) as stand-ins for a hero “limited-edition/collectible pressing” tier, since higher-priced, brand-recognizable items tend to anchor a category page and reward rich-result schema (price, rating, availability) in search. Bottom line: I have no live web access, so this is general SEO/pricing reasoning, not verified vinyl data — a real keyword mine would need a live crawl of Discogs sold listings, eBay comps, and Bandcamp/indie record-shop sites to get actual genre demand and pressing-condition modifiers like “180g,” “first pressing,” or “reissue.”
